title: Preference Pair Generation
definition: The process of creating a dataset consisting of preference pairs (a chosen response and rejected responses) for training a language model, focusing on minimizing drifts in the generated responses.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Creating a set of examples where a good response is chosen and less good responses are rejected to help a computer model learn what kind of answers are most appropriate in a given context.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Generating a dataset of preference pairs (chosen and rejected responses) to train a language model, focusing on minimizing drifts in the generated responses and improving the model's performance on specific tasks or domains.
difficulty_levels.expert: Utilizing preference pair generation to create a dataset of training examples for a language model, focusing on minimizing drifts in the generated responses and improving the model's performance on specific tasks or domains by leveraging held-out prompts from the previous step and hand-written probes.

extra_fields.insight: Creating preference pairs to train a language model, ensuring it generates responses that are consistent and appropriate for specific tasks or domains.
